newsitem.title: USA: Harrison Ford admits he dodged Vietnam War draft.
newsitem.headline: Harrison Ford admits he dodged Vietnam War draft.

text.p: In the "Star Wars" and "Indiana Jones" movies, he played brave adventurers, but in real life Harrison Ford avoided fighting in the Vietnam War by claiming to be a conscientious objector, the actor said.

In an interview in the July edition of "Movieline" magazine, Ford acknowledged he dodged the draft during the late 1960s when he was a struggling actor just out of college. Asked if he was classified as a "conscientious objector," he was quoted as saying no.
"I confused them (the draft board) so badly that they never took action on my petition," he said. "My conscientious objection wasn't based on a history of religious affiliation.
"I went back to my philosophy training at college," he said, explaining that he wrote a long thesis arguing about the concept of God as not a being but rather the most meaningful thing in his life.

"I always had trouble with the word or notion of God in a stand-up form. So I developed that thesis and took the biblical injuction to love thy neighbour as thyself as the central and most meaningful thing in my life.

"I combined it all and typed for days and sent it off and never heard a word," Ford told "Movieline." He said that more than two years later his first wife became pregnant and he was granted an exemption from serving his country.
